title: Past Experiences & Stories
description: Tell stories and describe past experiences using the preterite and imperfect tenses, with narrative connectors and time markers.

grammar.title: Preterite (Pretérito Indefinido) — Completed Actions
grammar.content:
The preterite is used for actions that are seen as completed in the past. It narrates specific events that happened at a definite time.

Regular preterite conjugations:

-AR verbs (hablar):
Yo hablé, tú hablaste, él/ella habló, nosotros hablamos, vosotros hablasteis, ellos hablaron

-ER verbs (comer):
Yo comí, tú comiste, él/ella comió, nosotros comimos, vosotros comisteis, ellos comieron

-IR verbs (vivir):
Yo viví, tú viviste, él/ella vivió, nosotros vivimos, vosotros vivisteis, ellos vivieron

Important note: -ER and -IR verbs share the same preterite endings. The difference between -ER and -IR appears only in the imperfect.

Time markers that signal the preterite: ayer, la semana pasada, el año pasado, hace dos días, en 2020, el lunes.
examples: Ayer hablé con mi amigo. (Yesterday I spoke with my friend.)
El año pasado viajé a España. (Last year I traveled to Spain.)
La semana pasada comimos en un restaurante. (Last week we ate at a restaurant.)
grammar.aid_note: In Romanian, past actions are expressed with the perfect tense (am vorbit, am mâncat) or the simple past (vorbi, mâncăi — literary). Spanish uses the preterite (hablé, comí) for completed actions, which is a different concept. Spanish learners should focus on the time markers: if you say 'yesterday' or 'last week,' use the preterite.

grammar.title: Imperfect (Pretérito Imperfecto) — Background & Description
grammar.content:
The imperfect describes ongoing situations, habitual past actions, and background descriptions. It sets the scene for a story.

Regular imperfect conjugations:

-AR verbs (hablar): hablaba, hablabas, hablaba, hablábamos, hablabais, hablaban

-ER verbs (comer): comía, comías, comía, comíamos, comíais, comían

-IR verbs (vivir): vivía, vivías, vivía, vivíamos, vivíais, vivían

The three irregular imperfect verbs:
- ser: era, eras, era, éramos, erais, eran
- ir: iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, ibais, iban
- ver: veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veíais, veían

Use the imperfect for:
- Habits: Antes jugaba en el parque. (I used to play in the park.)
- Descriptions: Era un día bonito. (It was a nice day.)
- Ongoing actions: Mientras yo estudiaba, mi hermano dormía. (While I studied, my brother slept.)
- Age, time, weather: Tenía diez años. Eran las tres. Hacía frío.
examples: De niño, vivía en Madrid. (As a child, I lived in Madrid.)
Era muy temprano y hacía sol. (It was very early and the sun was shining.)
Siempre íbamos a la playa los sábados. (We always went to the beach on Saturdays.)
Mientras yo cocinaba, ella ponía la mesa. (While I was cooking, she set the table.)
grammar.aid_note: In Romanian, habitual past is often expressed with 'obicei' (I used to) or the imperfect (mergeam = I used to go). The Spanish imperfect has a similar function — both describe repeated or ongoing past actions. However, Spanish uses the imperfect much more broadly for descriptions and setting scenes, which Romanian expresses differently.

grammar.title: Preterite vs. Imperfect — The Key Decision
grammar.content:
Choosing between preterite and imperfect is one of the most important skills at A2 level.

Use the PRETERITE for:
- One-time completed actions: Ayer fui al cine. (I went to the cinema yesterday.)
- A series of completed actions: Me levanté, desayuné y salí. (I got up, had breakfast, and left.)
- Actions with a clear beginning and end: La película duró dos horas. (The movie lasted two hours.)

Use the IMPERFECT for:
- Ongoing background: El sol brillaba. (The sun was shining.)
- Habitual actions: Siempre caminaba al trabajo. (I always walked to work.)
- Descriptions: Era de noche y hacía frío. (It was night and cold.)
- Age, time, weather: Tenía cinco años. Eran las ocho. Hacía calor.

Key signal words:
- Preterite: ayer, anoche, la semana pasada, el año pasado, de repente, entonces
- Imperfect: siempre, normalmente, todos los días, cada semana, mientras

Both tenses together tell stories:
Cuando era niño, jugaba en el parque. Un día de repente encontré una moneda. (When I was a child, I used to play in the park. One day I suddenly found a coin.)
examples: Antes vivía en una casa pequeña. Un año pasado compré un apartamento. (I used to live in a small house. Last year I bought an apartment.)
Cuando era joven, viajaba mucho. Fui a treinta países. (When I was young, I traveled a lot. I went to thirty countries.)
Mientras cocinaba, sonó el teléfono. (While I was cooking, the phone rang.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian distinguishes past aspects differently — using the perfect tense for recent/narrative past and the imperfect for ongoing/repeated past. The Spanish preterite/imperfect distinction is more grammaticalized. Focus on the English equivalent: if the English translation uses simple past ('I went'), it's often the Spanish preterite; if it uses 'used to' or 'was/were + -ing', it's the Spanish imperfect.

grammar.title: Narrative Connectors — Structuring a Story
grammar.content:
Connectors help you organize a story logically. Spanish uses several connectors that signal the progression of events.

Time connectors:
- Primero... luego... finalmente... (First... then... finally...)
- Antes de eso... Después de eso... (Before that... After that...)
- Mientras... (While...)
- Cuando... (When...)

Story structure connectors:
- Al principio... (At first...)
- De repente... (Suddenly...)
- Entonces... (Then / So...)
- Por eso... (That's why...)
- Sin embargo... (However...)
- Al final... (In the end...)

Opening a story:
- ¿Sabes lo que pasó? (Do you know what happened?)
- Te cuento una historia... (Let me tell you a story...)
- La semana pasada me pasó algo interesante. (Something interesting happened to me last week.)

Continuing a story:
- Y entonces... (And then...)
- ¿Y qué pasó? (And what happened?)
- Después... (After that...)

Reactions:
- ¡Qué susto! (What a scare!)
- ¡No puedo creerlo! (I can't believe it!)
- ¿En serio? (Really?)
- ¡Qué bien! / ¡Qué mal! (How great! / How bad!)
examples: Al principio no estaba seguro, pero luego decidí ir. Finalmente fue una buena decisión. (At first I wasn't sure, but then I decided to go. Finally it was a good decision.)
De repente, sonó la puerta. Era mi amigo sorpresa. (Suddenly, the doorbell rang. It was my friend, a surprise.)

¿Sabes lo que pasó ayer? Primero llegué tarde, luego perdí las llaves y finalmente volví a casa sin poder entrar. (Do you know what happened yesterday? First I arrived late, then I lost my keys, and finally I got home without being able to get in.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian also has narrative connectors (mai întâi = first, apoi = then, brusc = suddenly, în cele din urmă = finally). The Spanish connectors are generally more transparent for Romanian speakers since Spanish connector vocabulary often has cognates (finalmente = în cele din urmă / final.

pronunciation.title: Narrative Pronunciation — Past Tense Endings
pronunciation.content:
Pronouncing the preterite and imperfect endings clearly is essential for being understood.

Preterite -AR endings (stress on the ending):
- hablé = AH-bleh (stressed) — the accent mark indicates stress
- hablaste = ah-BLS-teh
- habló = ah-BLÓ
- hablamos = ah-BLAMOS (stress on first A)
- hablasteis = ah-BLÁS-téis (stress on first E)
- hablaron = ah-BLÁ-ron

Preterite -ER/-IR endings (stress on the ending):
- comí = koh-MÍ
- comiste = koh-MÍS-teh
- comió = koh-MÍ-oh
- comimos = koh-MI-mos (stress on first I)
- comisteis = koh-MÍS-teis
- comieron = koh-MI-E-ron (stress on first I)

Imperfect endings (stress on the stem):
- hablaba = ah-BLA-bah
- comía = koh-MÍ-ah
- vivía = bee-BÍ-ah

Key pronunciation rules:
1. Preterite endings are STRESSED — the accent marks are guides
2. Imperfect endings are unstressed — the stem carries the stress
3. The -ió ending is pronounced as two syllables: -ee-oh
4. The -eron ending is pronounced as three syllables: -eh-ron
5. The 'ñ' in nosotros forms (hablamos vs. hablabamos) is the same sound as in 'señor'

Common mistakes:
- Don't add 'e' before consonant clusters: comí (not 'comee')
- The 'y' sound in comiste is like English 'y': koh-MYES-teh
- The 'll' in habló sounds like English 'y': ah-YÓ
examples: comí = koh-MÍ (like 'koh-MEE' with stress on second syllable)
fui = fwee (one syllable, like 'fw-ee' said together)
fue = fweh (one syllable, like 'fw-eh' said together)

exercises.question: Which tense do you use for a completed action that happened 'ayer' (yesterday)?
exercises.explanation: The preterite is used for completed actions with specific time markers like 'ayer' (yesterday). 'Ayer hablé con mi amigo' — yesterday I spoke with my friend.

exercises.question: Which tense do you use to describe what the weather was like in the past?
exercises.explanation: Descriptions of weather, age, time, and ongoing states use the imperfect. 'Hacía frío ayer' (It was cold yesterday).

exercises.question: Complete with the correct preterite form: 'Ayer yo ___ (hablar) con mi madre.'
exercises.explanation: Ayer (yesterday) signals the preterite. 'Ayer yo hablé con mi madre' = Yesterday I spoke with my mother.

exercises.question: Complete with the correct imperfect form: 'De niña, ella ___ (jugar) en el parque todos los días.'
exercises.explanation: De niña (as a child) + todos los días (every day) signals a habitual past action — use the imperfect. 'De niña, ella jugaba en el parque todos los días' = As a child, she used to play in the park every day.

exercises.question: Which connector means 'suddenly'?
exercises.explanation: 'De repente' means 'suddenly.' It's used to introduce an unexpected event in a story: 'De repente, sonó el teléfono' (Suddenly, the phone rang).

exercises.question: Complete with the correct connector: '___, llegué a casa. Luego, cociné la cena. Finalmente, me acosté.' (First, I got home.)
exercises.explanation: 'Primero... luego... finalmente...' is a common narrative structure: first, then, finally. 'Primero, llegué a casa. Luego, cociné la cena. Finalmente, me acosté.' (First, I got home. Then, I cooked dinner. Finally, I went to bed.)

exercises.question: Which sentence uses the preterite correctly?
exercises.explanation: 'Ayer comí una pizza' uses the preterite correctly. 'Ayer' (yesterday) signals a completed past action. 'Comía' would be imperfect (I used to eat), which doesn't match a specific time marker.

exercises.question: Which of these is a story-opening phrase?
exercises.explanation: '¿Sabes lo que pasó?' (Do you know what happened?) is a common way to start telling a story. The others are basic questions for introductions, not narrative openings.

exercises.question: Complete with the correct imperfect form of 'ser': 'Cuando era niño, yo ___ (ser) muy tímido.'
exercises.explanation: Describing personality in the past uses the imperfect. 'Era' is the imperfect of 'ser'. 'Cuando era niño, yo era muy tímido' = When I was a child, I was very shy.

exercises.question: In the sentence 'Mientras yo estudiaba, mi hermano dormía,' which tense is used for both verbs?
exercises.explanation: Both verbs are in the imperfect, describing two ongoing actions happening simultaneously. 'Mientras' (while) is a common signal for the imperfect.

exercises.question: Which verb is NOT one of the three irregular imperfect verbs?
exercises.explanation: The three irregular imperfect verbs are: ser (era), ir (iba), and ver (veía). 'Hacer' is regular in the imperfect: hacía, hacías, hacía, hacíamos, hacíais, hacían.

exercises.question: Complete with the correct preterite form of 'ir': 'El año pasado ___ (ir) a Madrid con mis amigos.'
exercises.explanation: 'Ir' is completely irregular in the preterite: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. 'El año pasado fui a Madrid' = Last year I went to Madrid.

exercises.question: What is the correct order of narrative connectors for telling a story?
exercises.explanation: The logical order is: primero (first) → luego (then) → finalmente (finally). This creates a clear narrative progression.

exercises.question: Complete with the correct preterite form of 'decir': 'Mi amigo me ___ (decir) una historia muy divertida.'
exercises.explanation: 'Decir' is irregular in the preterite: dije, dijiste, dijo, dijimos, dijisteis, dijeron. The third person singular is 'dijo'. 'Mi amigo me dijo una historia' = My friend told me a story.

exercises.question: Which phrase would you use to react to a surprising story?
exercises.explanation: '¡Qué susto!' means 'What a scare!' and is used to react to surprising or scary stories. The others express beauty, goodness, or friendliness.
